methodology: v2 adds an OPTIONAL, per-attribute age adjustment on top of v1's unchanged lambda/M (both were validated via nested held-out temporal testing first -- see the accompanying report). The age adjustment is a PREDICTIVE correction for the expected change in rate between season T and T+1 (fit on real training-period residuals only, tested on a real held-out period never used to fit it) -- NOT a discount applied to a player's current-season rating. Two forms used, chosen per-attribute by whichever won on held-out data: 'bucket' (age-bucket mean residual, additive) or 'linear' (weighted least-squares residual ~ age, additive). Attributes where neither model meaningfully beat no-adjustment on held-out data carry an empty adjustment (a real, tested null result, not an oversight).

temporal_validation.note: Base lambda/M were re-selected using ONLY train-period pairs (nested recalibration) and found to match the full-dataset fit exactly for 5 of 6 attributes (three_point differed only within a confirmed flat optimum, lambda 0.70 vs 0.85, MAE difference 0.0001). Age adjustments were fit on train-period residuals only and evaluated on the held-out period.

age_adjustment.unit: additive rate correction per year of age

age_adjustment.reason: No real held-out benefit found (0.0076 -> 0.0077, i.e. slightly WORSE) -- a real, tested null result. LOCK V1, no age adjustment.
Linear model gave a negligible +0.1% (0.0162 -> 0.0162, within noise) -- not adopted. LOCK V1, no age adjustment.

age_adjustment.note: Real, large systematic bias (over-prediction growing through the late 20s) -- a coarse patch over what Part D's STL/BLK decomposition shows is really TWO different aging processes (BLK's bias onsets earlier/steeper than STL's). Flagged for Phase 4: consider a two-component underlying model rather than relying on this single bucket correction long-term.

not_calibrated.ball_security: Still explicitly excluded, unchanged from v1.

stl_vs_blk_decomposition.conclusion: Different optimal M (500 vs 150) and different aging-bias onset (BLK's overprediction starts by age 22-24 at +0.025; STL's stays under +0.01 until age 26-28). Real evidence the combined defensive_playmaking attribute hides two distinct aging processes. NOT split into separate core attributes this phase -- the 18-attribute vocabulary is unchanged. Recommend Phase 4 consider representing defensive playmaking as one combined DISPLAY attribute generated from two latent components (STL ability + BLK ability), not a vocabulary change.
